paragraphs: (b) Son of Yosef; Yosef was a righteous convert [the pinned Heilprin text reads נר צדק], among Sisera's descendants. Yuḥasin, in Seder HaDorot, quotes R. Tarfon saying of him, 'Happy are you, Abraham our father, that R. Akiva descended from you.' But he was descended from converts; how from Abraham? Perhaps Yosef married an Israelite woman. Necessarily so: as academy head and intercalator of years, without an Israelite mother he would not meet 'from among your brothers'; see Shemayah. Asarah Ma’amarot (Ḥiqur Din 5:11) says R. Akiva came from Sisera's intercourse with Yael, wife of Ḥever the Kenite. Yet R. Akiva holds a gentile's child by an Israelite woman is a mamzer. Yalkut Yehoshua§9, however, calls Yael a convert: perhaps she converted after Sisera's intercourse—ז״ר [source unresolved].

(c) R. Akiva was born3760 (see part 1); destruction 3828: he was 68. Killed 3880, he lived 52 years afterward. Some say killed 73 years afterward, 3901. Living 120 years, he was born 3781, aged 47 at destruction. He taught forty years and sustained Israel forty years: how could they seek to appoint him nasi only three years after destruction, on removing Rabban Gamliel? Keritot's view, quoted under R. Yishmael the High Priest, gives Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai forty post-destruction years as nasi, then Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, removed three years later. R. Akiva was then 90, hence considered for the office. He began learning at 40 after marrying Kalba Savua's daughter. Modest before marriage and her father's shepherd (see his entry), he was prohibited by her father's vow from benefit. He studied ב״ד years [apparently 24; source numeral held], returning with 24, 000 students. His father-in-law had his vow released and received half his property, Nedarim 50a; Ketubbot 63a. Some say he came home after 24 years with R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua, aged 64, and only then married her. He apparently had an earlier wife, mother of R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah; see the necessary proofs there. He lived 120 like Moshe, Hillel and Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai. End of Sifrei and Vayeḥi Rabbah: forty years serving, forty sustaining Israel. Dorot Olam says he headed the academy after Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh; then Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, Rabbi's father.

(d) All those students died of askara between Passover and Shavuot for failing to honor one another. Another reading [ג״א, provisional]: until peras before Shavuot, fifteen days earlier, 18 Iyar, Lag BaOmer; marriage is then permitted. Mnemonic: 'At eighteen, the wedding canopy.' The world was desolate until R. Akiva taught our southern teachers: R. Meir, R. Yehudah, R. Yose—Sefer HaKavvanot, Omer gate, substitutes R. Neḥemyah—R. Shimon and R. Elazar ben Shammua, Yevamot 62b. Bereshit Rabbah, 'Avraham added,'61, adds R. Yoḥanan the Sandalmaker and R. Eliezer ben Yaakov. Another version: R. Yehudah, R. Neḥemyah, R. Meir, R. Yosef—should read R. Yose—R. Shimon ben Yoḥai, R. Ḥanina ben Ḥakhinai and R. Yoḥanan the Sandalmaker. A gloss in HaKavvanot: of seven students R. Meir was greatest, the Sandalmaker least, the sandal clothing R. Akiva's heel—Maharḥu [attribution held]. Tanḥuma, end of Ḥayyei Sarah: he had 300 students in youth, all died; without seven in old age, none would have been called after him. 'Until R. Akiva came and taught,' Shabbat 64b; Rosh HaShanah 17b; Nedarim 25b, 66a; Bava Metzia 62; Bekhorot 6b: he expounded 'The Lord your God' to include Torah scholars—see Neḥemyah HaAmsuni. 'Until R. Akiva expounded: your life takes precedence'; see Petirah above.

(e) At Benei Berak, Sanhedrin 32b. Called a stored treasury, or balum: he learned everything mixed together, then sorted each matter, Gittin 67a. He never declared study-house dismissal except Passover eve and Yom Kippur eve, Pesaḥim 109a. At his son's feast he said over each cup, 'Wine and life to the rabbis,' Shabbat 67b. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Keitzad Mevarekhin: at Shimon his son's feast, over each barrel, 'Good wine for rabbis and their students.' R. Yehoshua, R. Akiva's son, asked; some identify him with R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah (see there). Ben Azzai said all Israel's sages were like garlic peel before him except 'this bald one.' Halikhot Olam, gate 1, attributes this to R. Elazar ben Azaryah concerning R. Akiva: an error or omission. Tosafot Yesh Noḥalin, citing Megillat Setarim, says Ben Azzai meant bald R. Elazar ben Azaryah; see there and R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah. Shalshelet HaKabbalah 28b says academies called R. Akiva bald because his argumentation made the sages bald. Asarah Ma'amarot, ח״ה מח״ד§11 [division initials held], defends Ben Azzai's manners: sages greatly honored as Torah's protective peel; R. Akiva foremost, bald and pure, was the fruit, Oral Torah. שום in Atbash is בפ״י; see there. Keren Or, citing Me'orei Or, links baldness to 'I am a smooth man,' and 'From whose womb came this ice/baldness': מי, Binah, produced smooth Yaakov. Zohar Bereshit 87 [source עפ״ז] places baldness in Yesod and Yaakov's attribute as זה. Were I not afraid, I would compare Ta'anit 3b's sun between bald patches: Rashi, cloud here and light there; Tosafot, rain on either side and sun between, like hair and baldness. R. Akiva was bald through convert ancestry, luminous through himself, as above.

Yevamot 16a: R. Dosa ben Harkinas praised his world-spanning name, although he had not reached a cattle-herd's level. Jerusalem Talmud 1, halakhah 6, applies 'Young lions lack and hunger,' recognizing his Torah strength. He left none equal in the Land when going to Nehardea to intercalate years; see Ḥananyah, R. Yehoshua's nephew. For denying return to the wilderness generation and ten tribes, R. Yoḥanan said he abandoned his piety, Sanhedrin 110b. Humble and accepting rebuke, Arakhin 16b: R. Yoḥanan ben Nuri testified that his complaints to Rabban Gamliel often brought Akiva punishment, yet increased Akiva's love for him. Eruvin 53a compares earlier hearts—R. Akiva—to the Temple porch, later R. Elazar ben Shammua to its hall. Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:14:1’s later figures: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, R. Eliezer, R. Yehoshua, R. Akiva, R. Meir. He entered pardes and emerged peacefully, Ḥagigah 14. Mocking transgressors, he saw Satan as a woman atop a palm and climbed; halfway his impulse left. Without Heaven's warning to beware R. Akiva and his Torah, Satan would have made his blood worth two ma'ah, Kiddushin 81a. Avot deRabbi Natan 16: a ruler sent two adorned prostitutes; he ignored them, etc., finding their smell like carcasses and creeping creatures. He was administrator and treasurer for the poor, Kiddushin 1; Ma'aser Sheni 5; Rashi Bava Metzia 1; Keren Or, manner 3, explains why. Jerusalem Talmud, end of KeShem: R. Akiva identified Elihu ben Berakhel with Bilam. R. Elazar ben Azaryah said if so, God concealed him; if not, he would dispute with Akiva.

He followed R. Yehoshua into a privy and learned three things. Ben Azzai asked how he dared; Torah required learning. Ben Azzai then followed Akiva, and R. Yehudah likewise objected, Berakhot 62a; Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 9, halakhah 8 [9:5:12 in Sefaria]. Semaḥot 4, end; Jerusalem Talmud, Nazir 7:1; Derekh Eretz Zuta 8: R. Akiva called this his first merit before sages: he found a slain man, carried him three Sabbath boundaries and buried him. R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua called each step bloodshed. He reasoned: if intending merit he sinned, all the more without that intent. Kallah: elders saw two boys, one covering his head, one uncovering. R. Eliezer called the latter a mamzer; R. Yehoshua, son of a menstruant; R. Akiva, both. They asked how he dared contradict colleagues—perhaps modestly calling his teachers colleagues. He promised proof, finding the mother selling pulses. He offered the world to come for an answer. She demanded an oath; he swore aloud, annulled inwardly, and asked about her son. Menstruating at marriage, her husband withdrew; her wedding attendant had intercourse with her, producing him. R. Akiva's contradiction proved great; they blessed God for revealing His secret to R. Akiva ben Yosef. R. Tarfon said parting from him was parting from life; 'Happy Abraham, R. Akiva descends from you.' Shalshelet HaKabbalah 28b–29a says he knew seventy languages, apparently Rashi Sanhedrin 3; actually Sanhedrin 1.

Mo'ed Katan 21b: his sons died, all Israel eulogized them; their honor consoled him. Semaḥot 8: his learned son Shimon died; his assured place in the next world, learning and benefiting many consoled him. Nevertheless Akiva did not suspend study while he was ill until death. They brought a bench to the cemetery; he sat expounding all day. Walking in a cemetery he met a naked, coal-black man carrying wood, running like a horse. He stopped him: was he a slave to redeem, or poor to enrich? The man begged not to delay, lest his overseers rage. Dead, he was sent daily to gather wood and be burned in it. Formerly a tax collector, he favored rich and oppressed poor. Had he heard of release? Only an impossible thing: a son leading Kaddish, the congregation answering 'Amen, may His great name be blessed.' He left a pregnant wife, no known son, no friend to teach him. R. Akiva undertook the search: the man was Ukva, wife Shushiva, town Lanuka'ah. There people cursed his bones and her memory; the son was uncircumcised. R. Akiva circumcised him and taught him, but he could not bear Torah's yoke. After R. Akiva fasted forty days, a heavenly voice asked why. He had guaranteed the child before God. God opened his heart; Akiva taught Torah, Shema, the Amidah and Grace. He led Barekhu; the congregation answered 'Blessed is the blessed Lord forever and ever'; Kaddish received its answer, and his father was freed from Gehinnom. In a dream the father blessed R. Akiva's relief and rescue. R. Akiva recited 'Lord, Your name forever; Your remembrance generation after generation'—a small book. Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Zuta 18 has precisely such an incident with Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai; see Zikkukin DeNura.

In public prayer he shortened and finished, Berakhot 31a. Semaḥot 9: at his father's death others bared shoulders before him, but he did not. Rabban Gamliel saw R. Akiva's ship sink, grieved, then found him discussing law. A plank had come to him; he bowed his head to every wave, end of Yevamot; see R. Meir above. Rabban Gamliel, R. Elazar ben Azaryah and R. Yehoshua heard Rome's roar 120 mil away, and saw a fox from the Holy of Holies; they wept, R. Akiva laughed, Makkot 24a; Eikhah Rabbah. Matters hidden from Moshe were revealed to him, Bamidbar Rabbah 19. Eruvin 21b praises his old-age imprisonment: refusing food without handwashing, he preferred death to violating sages' words; see Yehoshua HaGirsi. See Pappos ben Yehudah's debate with him under the ban on Torah study. Maimonides, end of Mishpatim, calls him armor-bearer of ben Koziva, Betar's king, whom he thought Messiah; see Part I, 3802 [the parallel is under 3880 in the digital transcription].

(f) Poor, he grew wealthy from six things, Nedarim 50a: (1) Kalba Savua, his father-in-law, above. (2) A ship's ram filled with gold dinars. (3) A chest of gold. (4) He and his students borrowed from a matron, with himself, God and sea as guarantors. On the repayment date he was ill. She addressed God at the shore: He knew R. Akiva could not pay, and was guarantor. The emperor's daughter went mad—Ran and Rosh; Rashi says the emperor—and threw jewels and gold into the sea. It brought the chest to her; she took it. Recovered, R. Akiva brought payment. The guarantor had repaid, she said, giving him the excess. (5) Turnus Rufus's wife. R. Akiva repeatedly defeated her husband through Scripture before the emperor. Returning gloomy, he explained why. She proposed tempting R. Akiva, since Israel's God hated sexual immorality. Beautifully adorned, with permission she exposed her leg before him. He spat, laughed and wept. Asked why, he explained two things but not the third—Rashi says her insistence elicited it. Spitting: her origin in a putrid drop; weeping: beauty decaying in earth. Laughing: holy inspiration showed her conversion and marriage to him, which he withheld. She asked whether repentance was possible; he said yes. She converted, married him and brought wealth. (6) Ketia bar Shalom—ש״ק29a calls him the emperor's converted minister—who gave all his wealth to R. Akiva and his students, Avodah Zarah 10b. Defending Israel, he was sentenced to death; he circumcised himself before death and left everything to R. Akiva and colleagues. R. Akiva expounded: half to Aharon, half his sons. He made his wife a golden Jerusalem ornament, Shabbat 59. He honored the wealthy, Eruvin 86a.

(g) R. Eliezer taught him magically planting cucumbers; he later learned it from R. Yehoshua, Sanhedrin 68a. He said his Sabbath sojourn—first Passover, source gloss—was with R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua, when he kneaded wine-and-honey dough without objection, Pesaḥim 36a. R. Eliezer permitted him to recite the blessing [Berakhot 37a names Rabban Gamliel]. He observed Rabban Gamliel and R. Yehoshua, Sukkah 37b; debated before Rabban Gamliel, asking instruction, Pesaḥim 48b. R. Akiva and R. Yishmael are 'fathers of the world,' beginning of Shekalim 3; Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh HaShanah 1, end of halakhah 1. R. Yishmael said to tell R. Akiva he erred, Yoma 75a [75b in the cited Bavli text], and asked him, Bereshit Rabbah 1, 22, 53; see R. Yishmael the High Priest. Heilprin cites Rashi in HaZahav as calling R. Akiva a student of Beit Shammai [the gloss is in HaMafkid, Bava Metzia 37b]. Tosafot disagrees. He served Naḥum Gam Zu 22 years, Ḥagigah 12; Shevuot 26a; Bereshit Rabbah 1, 22, 53. Naḥum said 'This too for good'; R. Akiva, everything from Heaven is good, Berakhot 60b. He learned Torah secrets from R. Neḥunya ben HaKanah—I do not know the source. Avot's 'All is foreseen, permission given' shows his knowledge of secrets. He learned somewhat from R. Tarfon, but was called colleague (see there). R. Yehoshua invoked Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, 'R. Akiva your student,' Sotah 23b [27b in the cited Bavli text]; he was a student's student; see R. Yehoshua ben Horkenos. He turned Rabban Gamliel and R. Yehoshua's silver into gold, Ma'aser Sheni 2:7. R. Yehudah: sitting before R. Akiva when Tisha BeAv fell Friday, Akiva swallowed a soft-cooked egg to demonstrate the fast was not completed, Eruvin 41a. Tallest in his generation, R. Meir reached his shoulder, Bamidbar Rabbah 9; see Abba Shaul. R. Elazar ben Azaryah precedes R. Akiva despite R. Akiva's importance as sages' head, because of pedigree and office, Tosafot Ketubbot 105a. Maharit asks why Yoma's life-saving discussion puts R. Akiva first; it must predate R. Elazar's appointment. Yet R. Tarfon appears after R. Akiva though, even if colleague, much older. End of quotation. His student Ben Azzai precedes him, Tosafot Sotah 4a; see the general rules.

(h) Anonymous Mishnah: R. Meir; Sifra: R. Yehudah (see Abba Arikha); Sifrei: R. Shimon; Tosefta: R. Neḥemyah; Seder Olam: R. Yose. All follow their teacher R. Akiva, Sanhedrin 86. Makkot 17a calls him Setimta'ah: Rashi, Rabbi habitually leaves his views anonymous; Bekhorot 30a. Shalshelet HaKabbalah 28b attributes מכילתין [work designation unresolved] and Sefer Yetzirah to R. Akiva, distinguishing Abraham's Sefer Yetzirah with Naḥmanides' commentary. Siftei Yeshenim and the Zohar introduction, R. Yitzḥak deLattes's ruling, call them one. R. Akiva visited Ganzik, Avodah Zarah 34a; Tosafot reads Mar Ukva, since R. Akiva would not be uncertain. There 39a has R. Akiva at Ginzak; Bereshit Rabbah 33, at Median Ginzak.

(i) The law follows R. Akiva against his teacher R. Eliezer in Keitzad Mevarekhin: Keritot, Yemot Olam, gate 3§4, Berakhot 36a; see Rava's ruling. Against R. Yishmael, R. Akiva prevails: Tosafot Yom Tov, Eduyot 2; Rif, Yevamot 15 and Kiddushin 1, and Rosh there [the parallel rulings cited by Ḥavvot Yair concern R. Tarfon]; see R. Tarfon's rulings. The law follows R. Akiva against a colleague, Eruvin 46b, Tosafot 65b; Ketubbot 84b excludes his teacher. Tosafot Yom Tov, Nega'im 1:4, excludes colleagues in the plural; likewise Responsa Sha’ar Efrayim [Heilprin cites §169, 295c. The parallel rule is in question 129 in the digital text. Ḥavvot Yair cites §169, fol. 95c.]. Yet end of Shevi'it 1 and Tosafot Yoma 4b imply even plural colleagues, as Tosafot Pesaḥim 116b states. Ḥavvot Yair: even so, this means individuals, not the sages collectively. Maimonides rules like R. Akiva against R. Eliezer ben Yaakov (see there). Sedeh Yehoshua limits the colleague rule to a named disputant in Mishnah/baraita; an anonymous view represents the majority, which defeats the individual. Yuḥasin, Rema's gloss on Raavad's tradition, quotes Maimonides' contemporaries of R. Akiva: R. Tarfon, R. Elazar of Modi'in, R. Elazar ben Azaryah, R. Yishmael, R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah, Ḥananyah of Ono, Shimon ben Nannas, R. Yoḥanan ben Berokah and R. Yishmael his son, R. Yoḥanan ben Gudgada, R. Elazar Ḥasma, R. Yehudah ben Tema.

(j) Rabbi was born the day he died, Kiddushin 72b; Kohelet, 'The sun rises'; Bereshit Rabbah, Noaḥ. At his death Torah's honor ceased, end of Sotah, Eglah Arufah 49; the Gemara, its strength ceased and wisdom's springs closed. Avodah Zarah 5a: God showed Adam each generation's interpreters; he rejoiced at R. Akiva's Torah, grieved at his death. Menaḥot 29b: Moshe was shown R. Akiva generations later, sitting behind eighteen rows [eight in the cited Bavli text] to hear him. Asked his source, Akiva answered a law to Moshe at Sinai, gladdening Moshe. He expounded heaps of laws from every crown. Moshe then saw his flesh weighed in butchers' stalls—Rashi, as Berakhot 61b's iron combs. 'This Torah and this reward?' God answered, 'Silence; thus arose in My thought.' Ministering angels in Berakhot asked likewise, receiving 'From men by Your hand, Lord, from men of this world,' rather than Moshe's answer. R. Eliezer told him: by slaughter you answered me; by slaughter you shall die; Pesaḥim 69a; Sanhedrin 68, before R. Eliezer's death.

Shalshelet HaKabbalah, fol. 31, says he was imprisoned 5 Tishri. Shenot Ḥayyim, Ḥayyei Sarah, cites a midrash: killed on Yom Kippur, returned to prison under guard against burial, until after Yom Kippur Elijah set aside priesthood for his honor and buried him. Yalkut Mishlei 9 at length: cave at Antiparos [Antipatris of Kotzrin in Yalkut Shimoni]. Gelilot Eretz Yisrael: Tiberias, above a cave, 24, 000 students scattered in its territory. Semaḥot 8: killed at Caesarea, also called Little Rome, a tower of Tyre. On hearing, R. Yehudah ben Bava and R. Ḥanina ben Teradyon tore garments: not robbery or deficient study caused death, but to spare him seeing evils. Within twelve months no place in Judea lacked slain people. Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah, ch. 5, halakhah 7 [5:5:6 in Sefaria], and Tosefta KeShem [Heilprin’s attribution, unresolved]: tried before wicked Turnus Rufus, he recited Shema and laughed. Asked whether foolish or defying suffering, he answered, 'May [your spirit] expire,' etc.

The prayerbooks' ten martyrs appear contemporary with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel; not so. Rabban Shimon died at destruction, R. Akiva nearly sixty years later. The last five—R. Yehudah ben Bava, R. Ḥanina ben Teradyon, R. Simai (source flags a scribal error and says 'should read' without supplying a name), R. Ḥutzpit, R. Yeshevav the scribe—were at Betar's conquest 73 years afterward; see part 1, 3880, and Baḥya, Mikketz. Earlier Yuḥasin gives R. Akiva until Betar 52 years after destruction, or 73 per סדר עולם [ס״ע, provisional]; see Aquila the convert. Akiva was first among ten—meaning principal, hence 'R. Akiva and colleagues.' At execution time, Shema, he lovingly accepted Heaven's yoke. Students asked, 'Even this far?' All life he longed to fulfill 'with all your soul,' even when taking it; now he would. He prolonged eḥad until his soul left; a voice blessed his departure in eḥad, Berakhot 61b. See R. Yishmael ben Elisha the High Priest and R. Ḥanina ben Teradyon for their deaths. Five instructions to R. Shimon ben Yoḥai, seven to his son, Pesaḥim 112.

(k) R. Akiva created converts' souls, his root from Kayin, like Abaye and Ben Azzai; see Abaye and Shammai; Ḥesed LeAvraham, spring 5, river 25. Ari's Kavvanot: reincarnation of Yaakov, letters עקיב; Yalkut Reuveni, Vayishlaḥ, initials of 'אל יעקב קום עלה בית אל' give עקיבא; see Vayeshev too. ריא״ז [Heilprin’s attribution] doubted whether to spell Akiva with alef or he. Heilprin reports that a dream showed 'אור זרוע לצדיק ולישרי לב שמחה,' final letters ר׳ עקיבה. Nof 3 of Nof Etz Ḥayyim: Yaakov shepherded father-in-law Lavan's flock, R. Akiva Kalba Savua's. Two wives: the daughter parallels Raḥel, Turnus Rufus's wife Leah. I think he had a wife before Kalba Savua's daughter; see R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah. R. Akiva was Moshe's spark, shepherd of Yitro; Tzipporah parallels the daughter, the Cushite queen Turnus Rufus's wife. Kalba Savua's vow parallels 'Moshe consented.' His statement 'This verse came to my hand' concerns Timna as Shema: Yaakov's refusal of Timna required repair. Vayeḥi: wife=Raḥel, 'ewe after ewe'; see R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah, her name Raḥel.

Emek HaMelekh 40b: R. Akiva was Zimri ben Salu, Simeonite ancestral head, in the account of the 24, 000 circumcised men slain at Shekhem, hence 24, 000 killed for sexual sin with Zimri; their reincarnations were R. Akiva's 24, 000 students. Asarah Ma'amarot, Ma'amar Em Kol Ḥai§22: R. Akiva was Shimon, R. Eliezer Reuven. ר״צ [work held] says Yissakhar. Megalleh Amukot, ofanim 73 and 88: as Leah went to Yaakov, producing Yissakhar, Yael met Sisera, producing R. Akiva. חס״ל5:25: Zimri's soul repaired in R. Akiva; Kozbi was Izevel, repaired as Turnus Rufus's wife. Izevel pursued Elijah/Pinḥas for revenge. Zimri was Dinah's son before Shimon married her;24, 000 Simeonites became R. Akiva's students, failing to honor one another because Shittim's sin remained, dying a second death. End of quotation.

Megalleh Amukot, ofan 73: six sources of wealth signify the six orders of the Oral Torah; R. Akiva expounded vavs throughout Torah, Yevamot 68b; Tosafot Sanhedrin 50b. He told R. Yishmael 'My brother, I expound bat and u-vat,' Sanhedrin 51b: brother in reincarnation, R. Yishmael=Yosef, R. Akiva=Shimon; see R. Yishmael ben Elisha. At first they did not recognize him; later he repaired brotherhood through vav. Moshe forgot the hooks, ווי העמודים, and could not reconcile the account until R. Akiva's soul came upon him: 'With the thousand he made hooks,' etc. Expounding every et—see above—signifies 'He brought Shimon out to them'; see Neḥemyah HaAmsuni. Dots over 'They went to pasture their father's flock' hint at this. Dying in eḥad, he reached love's palace, Zohar, Pekudei 2:254b [Heilprin’s pagination reads 456; the Zohar has ve-ahavta, while the Bavli has eḥad]. HaKavvanot, 'Yissakhar is a strong-boned donkey': R. Akiva wished in ignorance to bite a scholar like a donkey, Pesaḥim 49b; see R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah. He was in Esav's heel; Yaakov grasped it and took R. Akiva. עקבו contains vav R. Akiva, who expounded vav, Ari's writings; see R. Elazar ben Ḥarsom. The divine name's vav means wealth, hence six sources.

(l) R. Oshaya son of R. Yehudah the perfumer testified before him. R. Aḥa in his name. R. Eliezer ben Horkenos, his teacher. R. Elazar ben Azaryah in his time (see above). R. Elazar ben Shammua. R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, his student. R. Elazar Ḥasma. R. Elazar of Modi'in. R. Elazar ben Pila or Pavi answered his words. Baltza asked him. R. Berekhya in his name. Rabban Gamliel, his teacher. R. Dosa ben Harkinas (see above). Zonin spoke to him. R. Ḥidka. R. Ḥanina ben Antigonos. Ḥanan ben Pinḥas. R. Ḥanan ben Pattom. Ḥananyah of Ono in his name. R. Ḥananyah ben Ḥakhinai. R. Ḥananyah ben Akashya. R. Tarfon, his teacher or colleague (see there). R. Yehudah. R. Yehudah ben Beteira [ריב״ב; contextual expansion] told him, “Akiva, you will have to give an account.” R. Yehudah bar Ilai. R. Yehudah bar Abba disagrees. R. Yehudah Gelustera. R. Yehudah bar Neḥemyah (see there). R. Yehoshua HaGirsi, his attendant. R. Yehoshua ben Korḥah, his son (see there). R. Yehoshua ben Kefusai, his son-in-law. R. Yehoshua, his teacher, Shabbat 39. R. Yoḥanan ben Gudgada and R. Yoḥanan ben Matya in his time. R. Yoḥanan ben Nuri, his colleague. R. Yoḥanan ben Torta. R. Yoḥanan the Sandalmaker (see above). R. Yoḥanan in his name. R. Yonatan son of R. Yose, his student. R. Yonatan ben Yosef in his time. R. Yose the Galilean, student-colleague (see there). R. Yose (see above). R. Yannai the earlier in his time. R. Yaakov, Elisha's daughter's son. R. Yeshevav the scribe, his colleague. R. Yishmael, his colleague. R. Yishmael ben Loga spoke to him. Rav Kahana in his name. Levi HaSaddar in his time. R. Meir, his student (see above). Monbaz before him. Minyamin the Egyptian convert. R. Neḥunya ben HaKanah, his teacher. Naḥum Gam Zu, his teacher. Shimon HaShikmoni. R. Shimon HaTimni. Shimon, his son (see above). R. Shimon ben Elazar, his student—requires examination. R. Shimon ben Yehudah in his name. Rav Sheshet in his name.
